name: Bunbury Airwave
shape_type_notes: Not a V/delta/chevron/linear/crescent/L shape -- a single circular inflatable dome ('mound') with no arms or directional geometry.
coords: metres; origin = shoreline point nearest the reef centroid; x = alongshore (positive toward north, approximate -- Back Beach's coastline trends roughly N-S; no source gives an exact shoreline azimuth); y = offshore (positive seaward); shoreline approximated as the line y=0. Orientation is moot for a circle.

crest_depth_m.datum: below the water surface at low tide (LAT, approximate)

crest_depth_alt_note: Structure height above seabed is reported as 2 m in most contemporaneous sources (R1,R2,R3,R6) but as 1.6 m in one 2022 retrospective (R8); the 1.0 m crest-depth figure is a directly stated quote independent of which height figure is used.

distance_offshore_m.measured_from: shoreline (design target range 30-45 m; 37.5 m is the midpoint)

orientation_notes: None -- the reef is a radially symmetric circular dome (12 m diameter in all directions), so it has no arms, apex, or preferred alongshore/offshore axis.

volume_m3.method: estimated (not published): spherical-cap geometry V=(pi*h/6)*(3a^2+h^2) with base radius a=6 m, height h=2 m
volume_m3.uncertainty: +/-20%; cross-checked for plausibility against the stated 140-tonne sand fill (R8): 140 t / 117.3 m3 ~ 1.2 t/m3, a plausible bulk density for saturated sand+air fill

materials: Dome-shaped inflatable rubber (Hypalon, 5 mm thick) bladder with glued (not welded) seams; anchored to the seabed by partially filling it with sand, the rest of the bladder filled with water and air (R3: "The bladder is anchored to the seabed by partially filling it with sand. The rest of the bladder is filled with water and air."); total sand fill 140 tonnes (R8). Corrected 2026-09-25: an earlier draft quoted this as "washed, coarse beach sand" and omitted the water component -- that exact phrase does not appear on the R3 page and has been replaced with the verbatim quote.

derivation.uncertainty: +/-0 (repeated identically across 4 independently re-verified sources; R2 was re-checked 2026-09-25 and does NOT state a diameter/width figure at all -- dropped from this citation list)

derivation.method: stated in text (majority figure; one later source gives 1.6 m instead)
derivation.quote_or_figure: two-metre-high...dome-like bladder (R1); a 2-metre high, dome-shaped bladder (R2); rises about 2m (6.5 feet) off the sea floor at its highest point (R3)
derivation.uncertainty: conflicting alt. value 1.6 m in R8 (2022 retrospective). R6 (The Inertia) was re-fetched 2026-09-25 via a Wayback Machine snapshot (live site returns HTTP 403) and actually reads "about 7-feet high and 40-feet wide" -- an approximate, rounded imperial paraphrase (7 ft = 2.13 m), not the precise "6.5 feet" conversion of 2.0 m an earlier draft of this file incorrectly attributed to it. R6 is therefore downgraded from a precise cross-check to a loose corroboration and removed from this row's primary source_ref (kept for diameter, where 40 ft = 12.19 m rounds cleanly to 12 m).

derivation.method: computed: pi*(12/2)^2 from stated diameter, shape confirmed circular via aerial photo
derivation.quote_or_figure: 12 m diameter (text) + near-perfect circular footprint visible in aerial drone photo
derivation.uncertainty: +/-5% (assumes true circle); recomputed 2026-09-25 with python: pi*6^2 = 113.097 m2, rounds to 113.1 -- confirmed correct

derivation.quote_or_figure: at low tide, the shallow point is about 1m under the surface of the water
derivation.uncertainty: +/-0.2 m (about 1m); design condition, never verified as-installed

derivation.method: stated in text as a range (30-45 m); 37.5 m = midpoint
derivation.quote_or_figure: designed to be installed 30-45 meters off the beach
derivation.uncertainty: +/-7.5 m (half the stated range); as-installed position never surveyed. R2 was re-fetched 2026-09-25 and confirmed to NOT mention any offshore-distance figure at all -- dropped from this citation (an earlier draft of this file wrongly cited R2 alongside R3 for this number).

derivation.quote_or_figure: single diameter figure (not length x width) + circular aerial photo

images_relied_on.what_it_is: Aerial/drone photo of the inflated Airwave bladder just under the water surface off Bunbury Back Beach, Dec 2019 (already listed in our card's images array)
images_relied_on.what_was_read_off_it: Confirmed the plan-view footprint is a near-perfect circle (not oval/rectangular), corroborating the text's single-diameter (12 m) description. No scale bar present; size was not pixel-measured from this image, only shape.

images_relied_on.what_it_is: Waveco's 3D perspective concept rendering of the dome and the wave it is meant to shape (already listed in our card's images array)

disagree.why_ours: R3 (raisedwaterresearch.com, re-fetched 2026-09-25) states directly: 'at low tide, the shallow point is about 1m under the surface of the water.' No source supports 1.8 m. Traced Gemini's own working: its `reef_footprints.json` gives `coastal_context.ambient_seabed_depth_m = 3.8` and `crest_depth_m = 1.8` with the note 'Dome inflated to 2m height; crest submerged 1.8m' -- i.e. Gemini computed 3.8 - 2.0 = 1.8, but the 3.8 m 'ambient seabed depth' input is not sourced anywhere in Gemini's own files or ours; it appears to be an assumed/invented figure, not a cited one. Gemini's own two cited sources for this reef (a 2019 'project brief' and a 2020 Surfer Magazine review) do not appear anywhere in our reference list or in the pages we located, so they could not be independently checked.

R3 states a 30-45 m design-target range, not a single figure; R2 was re-checked 2026-09-25 and does not mention any offshore distance at all (an earlier draft of this file incorrectly cited R2 alongside R3 for this number). Gemini's 38 m happens to fall inside R3's range but is not itself sourced anywhere we could find (Gemini's own polygon in `reef_footprints.json` is simply centered at y=38, matching its stated value with no separate citation); we report the documented range's midpoint (37.5 m) instead of an unsourced point estimate.

open_issues: The reef was never completed (installation reached ~90% before a glued seam tore and the bladder was removed within days); every figure here is an as-designed value, not an as-installed/as-surveyed one.

Height above seabed is inconsistently reported: 2 m (R1,R2,R3 contemporaneous) vs 1.6 m (1 later retrospective, R8); R6's imperial 'about 7-feet' is an approximate corroboration only, not an independent precise measurement.

R3 and R9 in the verified card cite the same raisedwaterresearch.com URL under two different reference ids -- likely a minor duplication in the card, noted here but not corrected (out of scope for this footprint-only task).
No exact installed lat/lon or surveyed offshore distance exists; 30-45 m is the pre-installation design target, sourced to R3 only (R2 does not mention offshore distance).
Volume (117.3 m3) is our own geometric estimate, not a published figure; offered only as a sand-tonnage plausibility check.

Gemini's two cited sources for this reef ('Bottegal 2019 Project Brief', 'Surfer Magazine Trial Review 2020') could not be located or verified; treat Gemini's crest-depth and offshore-distance figures as unverified. Traced the specific mechanism of Gemini's 1.8 m crest-depth figure: it equals Gemini's own (unsourced) 3.8 m 'ambient seabed depth' input minus the 2.0 m height -- an internally consistent but externally unsupported calculation.

Attribution note: the earlier draft of this file's claim that Bunbury 'matches the flag already in Gemini's own suspicious notes' was imprecisely worded -- that 'suspicious' annotation ('one of the better-matched reefs') actually lives in OUR project's own intermediate extract file (07_scale/00_gemini_footprints_extract.json), not inside the Gemini folder itself. Gemini's own self-audit file (scale_sketch_photo_alignment_audit.md, row 11) independently marks Bunbury 'VERIFIED' with no discrepancy flagged. Both statements are substantively accurate; only the attribution of which file the note lives in has been corrected here.

Three citation errors found and fixed during 2026-09-25 adversarial verification: (1) R2 (ABC 2019-06-13) was wrongly cited alongside R3 for the 12 m diameter and the 30-45 m offshore distance -- re-fetched twice with targeted prompts and confirmed R2 states ONLY the 2 m height, nothing else; (2) R1's diameter quote was wrongly given the '(40 feet)' parenthetical that actually belongs to R3 -- R1's real text is metric-only ('two-metre-high, 12-metre-wide'); (3) R6 (The Inertia) was quoted as giving a precise '6.5 feet' height when the actual (Wayback-Machine-verified, since the live URL 403s) text says 'about 7-feet high' -- a looser rounding. None of these fixes changed any headline number (12 m, 2 m, 1.0 m, 30-45 m all still hold on corrected citations), but the reference attributions have been corrected throughout. A fourth fix: the fill-material quote 'washed, coarse beach sand' was not actually found on the R3 page and has been replaced with the verbatim R3 quote (sand + water + air).
